hero.title: GREAT WORK ISN'T ENOUGH. THE CLIENT HAS TO FEEL HELD.
hero.body: I help small and mid-size agencies run client service properly — account leads who own the relationship, meetings clients look forward to, and no surprises before a renewal. Commercials come after the service is solid.

about.title: I'VE BEEN THE PERSON THE CLIENT CALLS AT 7PM
paragraphs: I spent fifteen years inside independent agencies — account manager, account director, then head of client services in a 60-person shop. I ran the QBRs, handled the escalations, and rebuilt more than one relationship that had quietly gone cold.

What I saw, repeatedly: accounts lost despite strong work. Not because the creative failed — because nobody was clearly running the relationship. Status calls with no point of view, feedback absorbed rather than shaped, and a sponsor who no longer knew what they were getting.
Client service is a craft, and it can be taught. I help your account leads get good at it — then, once that's steady, we look at the commercials underneath it.

rows.value: Client service challenges, looking under the hood of independent agencies

rows.label: Not a fit

services.title: THREE THINGS I GET ASKED FOR
services.body: These are the three areas I am usually asked to help with. Client service first, the commercial side once the relationship is steady. Most engagements start with one and pull in a second.

items.title: ACCOUNT LEADERSHIP
items.body: Help for your account leads on what they actually own and how to run it — a rhythm they keep, a point of view in the room, and a clear line between serving a client and being run by one. Usually where we start.
items.tags: ROLE DEFINITION · MEETING CADENCE · OWNERSHIP MAP

items.title: CLIENT COMMUNICATION
items.body: Practice for the conversations most teams put off — presenting work with conviction, shaping feedback rather than collecting it, bringing bad news early, saying no without losing the relationship. On real clients, not in role-play.

items.title: FINANCIAL HEALTH
items.body: A plain look at what the work actually earns — which clients pay for themselves, where the team is spread too thin, and whether what you charge still matches what you deliver. No new reporting tools, just numbers you can read and act on.
items.tags: WHAT EACH CLIENT EARNS · HOW THE TEAM IS USED · WHAT YOU CHARGE

approach.title: SIT IN, FIX ONE THING, HAND IT OVER

steps.title: SIT IN ON THE ACCOUNTS
steps.body: I sit in on your status calls and one QBR, read the last six months of client threads, and talk to three account leads and, where you allow it, two clients.

steps.title: FIX THE ONE THING
steps.body: We pick the single change the accounts will feel first — usually how meetings are run or who owns the relationship — and build it properly rather than reforming everything at once.

steps.title: HAND IT OVER
steps.body: Playbook, a two-hour session with the account team, and a 90-day check-in. If you need me after that, something didn't land.

quote.text: OUR CLIENTS STOPPED FEELING LIKE THEY HAD TO CHASE US.
quote.author: Managing Director, 45-person independent agency

engagements.title: THREE WAYS TO WORK TOGETHER
engagements.body: One problem, the whole picture, or the long haul. Most agencies start small and widen it once they see how I work. Scope and fee are agreed before anything starts — no hourly surprises.

plans.title: ONE PROBLEM
items: You have one thing that needs an answer — a client relationship, a team question, or a number that no longer works
I get properly briefed, then we work it through together with the people involved
A written recommendation you can act on straight away
Ends there unless you want more

plans.title: THE FULL LOOK
items: A structured look at the whole agency, from the client side inward

Client relationships, how the team is set up to run them, and the financial health underneath: what you earn per client, how well the team is used, what you charge, and which clients are quietly on their way out
The one or two systems that matter rebuilt with your team, not handed to them
Playbook, a session with the team, and a check-in once it has had time to settle

plans.title: STANDING PARTNER
items: An ongoing arrangement, reviewed as we go
A regular working session with you and your leads
On call when something needs a second opinion before it is said out loud
A recurring read on where each client stands, who might be drifting, and what the work actually earns

contact.title: LET US GET IN TOUCH
contact.body: Thirty minutes, no deck. We'll talk about what keeps you awake at night and discuss how we can figure it out. :)
